column9: Upper bound; COVID-era Chromebook distribution to all students; Marysville High checked out Chromebooks during March 2020 school closure; no pre-pandemic 1:1 evidence found
i-CAN initiative 2004; first SC district to give wireless personal computing devices to all HS students; $8M program; by 2018-19 all 20 schools wireless with grades 3-12 reported as 1:1
Fall 2016: one Chromebook per 6th-grader at four middle schools; expanded to 7th grade fall 2017; eventually grades 6-12; later added grades 1-5 with CARES funding
District operates BYOD policy and loaner Chromebook program; no evidence of district-issued 1:1 program; as of 2026 capital plan proposes $1M+ for Chromebooks and IT infrastructure upgrade
Fall 2012: iPads for grades 3-6 (1:1); fall 2013 expanded to K-2; by 2015 every K-6 student had an iPad (5,400 total); district is a well-known early Apple 1:1 adopter
Upper bound; district website references 'Student Device Care & Maintenance' and G-Suite; 2021 TEA report notes hotspots and laptops provided to families; no earlier launch date documented
Upper bound; September 2020 report noted district providing one Chromebook per family during COVID-19 NTI; no pre-pandemic 1:1 evidence found
Upper bound; district has dedicated Chromebook support page; COVID-19 distance learning began April 2020; no earlier district-wide 1:1 evidence found
Upper bound; Azusa High School has a Chromebook agreement policy page; COVID-era device distribution evident; no pre-2020 1:1 announcement found
Upper bound; Blended Learning 1:1 Agreement forms confirmed for 2021-22 school year; district issues Chromebooks to grades 2-12 for in-school and at-home use; COVID funds accelerated program

Upper bound; GFPS reported August 2023 that grades 7-12 now have dedicated Chromebooks; program facilitated with COVID funds; elementary (K-6) portion under Great Falls Elem District unclear—separate NCES unit
Anytime Anywhere Learning (AAL) Initiative; fall 2017 every 9th-grader received laptop; expanded through high school ($1.55M); program grew to grades 6-12
Upper bound; district uses district-managed Chromebooks with ClassLink; no dated source for pre-pandemic 1:1 rollout found
COVID-era rollout; all TK-12 students issued Chromebooks at start of 2020-21 SY (August 2020); returning students had devices from March 2020 closure
Upper bound; district has device distribution policy page; technology history dates to 1993 Project Explore but Chromebook 1:1 rollout date not documented; COVID-era distribution likely

Ordered June 2020; arrived May 2021; nearly 7,000 laptops distributed to middle and high school students by end of 2020-21 SY; final round of students received devices September 2021; annual refresh cycle maintained
Upper bound; middle school 1:1 Chromebook program with take-home devices; HS has loaner program; Smart Schools Bond Act funded network upgrades; exact launch year not found
Upper bound; K-1 iPad; grades 2-12 laptop; program described as 1:1 K-12; 5th-12th grade take-home; ITS page copyright suggests pre-2020 launch; no firm dated announcement found

Upper bound; San Antonio area district used Google Classroom/Meet for COVID-era distance learning April 2020; technology reservation calendar for Chromebooks/iPads on district site; no pre-pandemic 1:1 evidence

Upper bound; all grades 1-12 issued Chromebooks; grades 4-12 may take home; district describes 'extensive one-to-one learning environment for several years'; Smart Schools Bond Act network upgrades cited; no firm launch year found
Upper bound; district has 1:1 Chromebook program for students; high school media center Chromebook info page exists; COVID-era implementation likely; no pre-2020 launch date documented

Upper bound; CCPS approved first Chromebook purchase (Lenovo) for new consolidated high school in 2026; technology AUP references student devices; COVID-era 1:1 likely but no clear launch date documented

Upper bound; district self-describes as one-to-one with each student receiving a Chromebook for school and home use; classrooms upgraded with Clear Touch Boards; Emergency Connectivity Fund purchase of 500 Chromebooks in July 2022; no earlier launch date found
By 2016-17 all grades 4-10 had own Chromebook; 4th grade added for 2016-17 expansion; program was ongoing before that year; professional development for blended learning accompanied rollout
Fall 2017 district-wide; $1.2M annual investment; largest district in Ohio to go 1:1 at the time; grades 5-12 each get Chromebook (take-home daily); K-4 have shared iPad carts in classrooms
